newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares powered ahead on Wednesday cheered by Wall Street's second ever biggest gain ever in point terms and first quarter results from electronics giant Philips that exceeded market expectations.
The AEX index of 25 leading shares ended 10.25 points, or 1.37 percent, higher at 758.94, dented towards the close by profit-taking prompted by a weaker start to Wall Street.
"Philips was the real eye-catcher today, but other stocks -- Royal Dutch and Unilver also performed well," one dealer said.
Philips said pre-bourse that first quarter net profit from ordinary operations was up 22 percent at 460 million guilders.
The shares attracted all the early volume, surging around 10 percent to above 100 guilders, where profit-taking set in. They slipped back late in the session to end 5.90 higher at 97.00.
"There were a lot of people with targets at 100 guilders and we saw a bit of selling pressure up there," one dealer said.
Europe's biggest consumer electronics group said sales had pushed up three percent to 16.14 billion guilders and stated the company was on track to meet its profit targets.
"We were extremely pleased with this result and the progress that has been booked in the first quarter," ING Barings analyst Steven Vrolijk said.

Other well traded gainers in the index included banking groups ABN AMRO and ING responded to the overall index rise and put on 1.70 and 1.60 guilders to close at 132.60 and 76.50 guilders respectively.
Good demand from U.S. basd investors was cited as being behind strong performances from Royal Dutch and Uniliver, which both gained well in New York on Tuesday.

However, both stocks eased back at the end of the session after Wall Street opened lower. Royal Dutch closed up 2.70 guilders at 345.10 and Unilever ended 3.30 guilders firmer at 376.60, both well off their earlier highs.
Computer software firm Baan closed up 7.20 guilders at 97.50 amid good buying ahead of the release of the company's results later this evening.

Dealers said the index's move, which takes it nearer the all-time peak of 779.02 points -- reached on March 11 -- left the market in good shape. "Speaking from the charts, it looks good and we could see the highs reached again," one dealer said.
Technical analysts have said the market would face its next tough hurdle at around 770-775 points but the solid support at 740 points had now been confirmed.
